title: Police deputy commissioner Alvin Moh to take over as HTX CEO, Singapore News

 singapore Police deputy commissioner Alvin Moh to take over as HTX CEO
 He will concurrently be appointed deputy secretary for development at MHA, with both roles effective from Feb 1, 2027 Deputy Commissioner of Police Alvin Moh (left), 46, will take over from Chan Tsan (right), 53, as CEO of HTX from Feb 1, 2027. Moh will be concurrently appointed as deputy secretary for development at the Ministry of Home Affairs. PHOTO: Ministry of Home Affairs PUBLISHED ON November 10, 2026 5:57 PM BY Sean Ler Deputy Commissioner of Police for Operations (DC) Alvin Moh Tser Loong will be leading the Home Team Science and Technology Agency (HTX) and be appointed deputy secretary for development at the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) from Feb 1, 2027, the ministry announced on Tuesday (Nov 10).
 He will take over from Chan Tsan , who is relinquishing both appointments to head the Land Transport Authority from May 1, 2027.
 The incoming chief executive and deputy secretary has spent nearly 27 years in the Singapore Police Force, holding several key appointments, including as director of the Police Intelligence Department and Planning and Organisation Department.
 He was also senior director of the Joint Operations Group (JOG) at the ministry headquarters. 
 The 46-year-old is credited with strengthening the police's technological transformation across frontline and regulatory operations, community partnerships, and training.
 He oversaw the rollout of the report lodging co-pilot , an artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted chatbot that helps the public to lodge clearer police reports, and the operationalisation of beyond-visual-line-of-sight aerial patrol drone capabilities .
 In his roles as JOG senior director and police intelligence director, DC Moh had played key roles in the country's efforts to combat criminal harms, scams and money laundering.
 MHA said that these included the development and operationalisation of the Online Criminal Harms Act , legislative amendments to strengthen Singapore’s ability to enforce against money mule and money laundering activities , and enhancements to the police's capabilities to detect and disrupt scams.
 Pivotal role in transforming science and technology ecosystem
 The ministry also paid tribute to its outgoing deputy secretary and HTX chief executive Chan, saying he played a pivotal role in strengthening the Home Team's science and technology capabilities and transforming the associated ecosystem.
 These include the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority’s new clearance concept, which achieved the world’s first 100 per cent passport-less immigration clearance in 2024, and the Home Team Sustainment Centre, which strengthens asset readiness through predictive, data-driven and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled operations.
 Beyond the systems-level, HTX has also worked on projects that enable Home Team officers to maintain their tactical advantage with higher sensemaking, speed, surprise, and response, while maintaining safety.
 One example is the ongoing trials of weaponised unmanned systems such as armed drones and the jet-propelled manpack .
 MHA said that Chan has also led HTX to expand the frontiers of public safety science and technology, spearheading the AI movement, which accelerated the agency’s ambition to become an AI-first organisation that harness AI to deliver greater operational impact across the Home Team.
 He is also credited with strengthening the HTX’s research and innovation capabilities, through initiatives such as the establishment of the Forensic Innovation Research for Strategic Transformation (FIRST) Lab in 2024.
 The lab strengthened Singapore’s response to synthetic drugs and emerging crime.
 Under Chan’s watch, the Singapore Civil Defence Force also became the world’s first lifesaving force to deploy a cyborg cockroach for search and rescue operations. 
 He also oversaw the establishment of the Home Team Humanoid Robotics Centre in 2026 to advance AI and robotics capabilities for future operational needs.
 "Mr Chan has built up HTX’s capabilities, talent and technological edge, strengthening the Home Team’s ability to meet Singapore’s evolving public safety and security challenges. 
 "Under his leadership, HTX has become an integral and trusted science and technology partner to MHA," the ministry said.
